description: The Sound role's profile for fast kinetic type: music at a known tempo with one drop, a recorded effect on every hit, the music stopped dead on the end card.

tempo.teaser: 15 to 25 s at 160 to 175 BPM (drum and bass, phonk, breakbeat): a beat is 0.35 s, the shot length the style runs at
tempo.calmer: 30 to 45 s at 120 to 135 BPM: about 8 cuts per 10 s then means a cut every 2 beats

structure: a tense intro, one drop on a bar line where the film turns (the first colour flip or the first picture), body at a steady level, the music stops dead on the end card's first beat
fit: beats.py <track> --bpm <intended> --start <s> --window <s> --drop-beat <n>: the fitted tempo, the downbeat offset, the drops, and the music.start that puts the drop on film beat n

recorded.title: Uplifting Bass
recorded.measured: 134.0 BPM, grid strength 1.0, drop at 14.39 s (8.3 dB rise); start 7.226 puts the drop on beat 16

music.generated: Optional. Higgsfield MCP generate_audio when its catalog lists a music model (models_explore type audio): get_cost first, show the price, wait for a yes, then one run. Its prompt takes a tempo as words, not a number field, so the tempo is a claim: fit it with beats.py and trust the fit, never the prompt.

impact.note: Movie trailer epic impact: every punch shot, every strike

impact_big.note: Big cinematic impact: the hero landing

hit.note: Martial arts fast punch: a lighter hit, the second part of a shot

tick.note: Hard pop click: a run of cuts on the beat

whoosh.note: Cinematic whoosh fast transition: a whip

whoosh_big.note: Cinematic tunnel reverb woosh: the zoom through a letter

riser.note: Cinematic trailer riser: the charge before the first word

glitch.note: Small electric glitch: a struck thing dying

logo_hit.note: Movie logo intro impact: the end card, with the music stopped

levels.sfx: each effect is normalised to -1 dBFS before its gain, so a gain says where it sits against the others

gate: earshot critique on the encoded file; fix every [critical] and [major], or write down why a line stays
